title: The Girl Who Talked to the River
author: Léxi
desc: Fanta entend la voix du fleuve. Quand la sécheresse arrive, elle seule peut sauver son village.

p: In a village near the Comoé river, there lives a girl called Fanta. She is twelve years old, and she has a secret. She can hear the river talk.
It started when she was a little girl. One day, she put her hand in the water, and she heard a voice. It was soft and old, like a grandmother singing.
*Hello, little one,* said the river.
Fanta told her mother. Her mother laughed. "Rivers don't talk, Fanta. Go and get water."

So Fanta stopped telling people. But every morning, when she goes to get water, she talks with the river. The river tells her stories: about the fish, about the crocodiles, about the old kings who once lived on its banks.
And every morning, the river says the same thing at the end: *Be kind to me, little one, and I will be kind to you.*
One year, the rains don't come. The sun burns the fields. The maize dies. The animals are thirsty.
And the river becomes smaller and smaller. Every day, its voice is weaker.
*I am sick, little one,* the river whispers. *Men from the city are taking my water upstream. And they throw rubbish in me. I am dying.*
Fanta runs to the village chief. "The river is dying! Men are taking its water!"
The chief is an old man with a white beard. He looks at her kindly. "Fanta, it is the dry season. The river is always small in the dry season."
"No! The river told me! It is sick!"
The other villagers laugh. "The river told her!" But one person does not laugh: Fanta's grandmother, Mama Ténin.
That night, Mama Ténin calls Fanta to her hut.
"When I was young, I heard the river too," she says quietly. "My grandmother heard it. And her grandmother. It is a gift in our family. Only girls have it, and only when they are pure of heart."
"Why didn't you tell me?"

"Because people laugh. People are afraid of what they don't understand." Mama Ténin takes a small blue stone from an old box. "This stone comes from the bottom of the river. If you hold it, the river can show you what it sees."

Fanta holds the stone. She closes her eyes. And she sees: far upstream, there is a big new wall across the river. Behind the wall, there is a factory. Pipes take the water. Black smoke goes into the sky.
The next morning, Fanta and her grandmother walk upstream. They walk for two days. They sleep under the trees. Fanta talks to the river every hour. *Courage,* she tells it. *We are coming.*
On the third day, they arrive at the factory. A guard stops them. But Fanta does not give up. She asks to see the director.

The director is a young woman from Abidjan. She listens politely. When Fanta says that the river talks, she smiles. But when Fanta describes the village — the dead maize, the thirsty animals, the children who are sick from bad water — the director stops smiling.
"We didn't know there were villages downstream," she says. "Nobody told us."
"Now you know," says Mama Ténin.
The director keeps her promise. The factory opens the wall a little every day. It cleans its water before it goes back into the river. And it builds a well for Fanta's village.
When Fanta comes home, the river is bigger. And its voice is strong again.
*Thank you, little one,* it sings. *You were kind to me. Now I will be kind to you.*
That week, the rains finally come. Heavy, warm, wonderful rain. The children dance in the mud. The maize grows again.
The village chief comes to Fanta's house. He bows his head. "Fanta, the village was wrong to laugh at you. From today, you are the guardian of the river."
Fanta goes down to the water. She puts her hand in it, like every morning.
*Hello, little one,* says the river.
"Hello, old friend," says Fanta. And she smiles.
